title: F1’s $3.2 Billion Las Vegas Legacy Sets The Stage For Luxury Brands To Up Their Game In 2026
Haas confirm Camara will finish 2026 season with the team
article_text:
Brazilian driver Rafa Camara will complete the 2026 season with Haas ahead of his full rookie season in 2027, the team confirmed on Sunday.

Formula 2 championship leader Camara took the place of ousted Esteban Ocon in Brazil and continued in the seat at this week's Las Vegas Grand Prix.

He will race for the team in Qatar on Nov. 29 and Abu Dhabi on Dec. 6. The Ferrari junior had already been confirmed to be replacing Ocon in 2027, but the Frenchman's sudden sacking during the Mexico City Grand Prix accelerated his F1 debut.

Haas' decision will likely cost Camara the chance to be F2 champion. F1's main feeder series will finish its own championship four races spread across the schedule in Qatar and Abu Dhabi -- Camara holds a slender seven-point lead over Red Bull junior Nikola Tsolov, with Alpine junior Alex Dunne 18 points back.

Team boss Aayo Komatsu said the opportunity for Camara to embed further into the team was too good to turn down. "We're excited to be able to finish the season with Rafa driving and build on his first two race starts with the team in Brazil and America," Komatsu said.

"I'm delighted that Rafa's embraced every track session as a learning opportunity and embedded himself further within the team. We now get to finish the season together which is advantageous to all of us ahead of a relatively short off-season and as our 2027 preparations get underway."

Haas had one other option if they had wanted Camara to finish off his F2 campaign -- reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa filled in for Ocon in Mexico City and scored a top-ten finish on his debut.

Camara will keep driving alongside fellow Ferrari junior Oliver Bearman in the final races. Although it is expected to be completed soon, Bearman has not had a new Haas deal confirmed yet.

Bearman is understood to be in talks with Ferrari about their wider plans for his career, mindful of what happens with him should Lewis Hamilton extend his stay with the team beyond 2027.

title: TTFA explores development partnership with Aspire Academy
article_text:
In what is hoped will be a significant step towards advancing sporting development in Trinidad and Tobago, president of the Trinidad and Tobago Football Association (TTFA), Kieron Edwards, and Secretary of Youth Empowerment and Sport in the Tobago House of Assembly (THA), Assemblyman Keigon Denoon, are in Qatar holding high-level discussions with Ivan Bravo, Director General of the world-renowned Aspire Academy.

The discussions are focused on exploring strategic partnerships and major sporting development initiatives aimed at strengthening youth development, elite athlete training, coaching education, sports infrastructure and international opportunities for athletes across Trinidad and Tobago.

Aspire Academy, internationally recognised for its world-class sporting facilities, talent identification and athlete development programmes, represents a valuable potential partner in the continued transformation of the nation’s sporting landscape.

The engagement signals a shared commitment to move beyond traditional approaches to sporting development by pursuing international partnerships that can unlock opportunities, develop local talent and establish sustainable pathways to sporting excellence.

“Our ambition must be bigger than simply producing talented athletes. We must build the systems, partnerships and opportunities that allow our talent to compete and succeed on the world stage,” said Edwards.

Via a release yesterday, the TTFA said it views these discussions as an important step towards building a stronger sporting future for Trinidad and Tobago, with particular emphasis on empowering the next generation of athletes.

title: Liam Lawson ends 52-year F1 wait despite Las Vegas GP misery
article_text:
Liam Lawson set the first fastest lap by a New Zealander in F1 since 1974 in a Las Vegas Grand Prix he almost did not start.

Just prior to the race, where he was due to start in seventh place, Lawson's Racing Bulls machine developed a fuel leak and was wheeled back into the garage for repairs - with the team able to get him back on track, having lost just one lap.

However, running by himself, Lawson was unable to latch onto the field in the slipstream-fest and had an otherwise lonely race, although he was joined briefly by Isack Hadjar's Red Bull after the front-wing failure required a new nose for the Red Bull.

Ultimately, Lawson finished in 15th on the road, but Hadjar was handed a 10-second time penalty for slowing down too much and holding up George Russell during the entry into the pit-lane, with Lawson promoted to 14th.

He had been just 0.100s behind Hadjar on the run to the line, with this tow aiding Lawson in setting the fastest lap of the race, a 1:35.591.

It is the fastest lap of Lawson's career, as he became the 142nd driver to set one, and the first for a New Zealander since Denny Hulme at the 1974 Belgian GP.

Overall, it is the 16th fastest lap by a New Zealander, and the first for Racing Bulls as a constructor, as it became the 46th squad to do so.

Reflecting on his evening, Lawson praised the team for its efforts in ensuring he had a quick machine after the fuel leak.

"I mean, that is really the big question," Lawson replied when asked by media, including RacingNews365, about when the fuel leak developed.

"What we need to answer is what we can do in the future to figure it out earlier, and we actually had a similar thing happen in Monaco this year - and both times the guys and girls have done a really, really good job to put the car together and maximise.

"For us to go out on track today and have absolutely no issue and have a really fast race car is massively impressive from everybody, and I just feel from them that I couldn't deliver because we lost a lap."

After the mid-race safety car, Lawson was allowed to unlap himself, but was not immediately released, meaning he could not catch the back of the pack for the restart.

Although he did earn the lap back under the safety car, Lawson was not able to latch onto the back of the pack for the restart as it took four laps to release him - something he expressed confusion at.

"I got it back, and we actually probably could have still had a really good race," he said.

"But I don't know why they took four laps to release me.

"I get that when there are marshals on the track, and there is safety around it; I can understand that, but it is still a double yellow.

"I can still slow for the double yellow zone and follow a delta; there is nothing stopping me. I'm not going to blow through that zone at high speed, but it means I can do the whole lap and catch back up.

"Unfortunately, they waited four laps, and then they gave me half a lap to catch back up, and I restarted 25 seconds behind the field."

title: 'The most chaotic race ever' – McLaren's Lando Norris reflects on remarkable recovery to P2 in Las Vegas Grand Prix
article_text:
Lando Norris reflected on an exceptionally chaotic Las Vegas Grand Prix after recovering from outside the points to finish second, securing a double podium for McLaren alongside team mate Oscar Piastri.

Lando Norris has described the Las Vegas Grand Prix as potentially the "most chaotic race ever in the history of Formula 1" after recovering from outside the points to claim second place and help secure a double podium for McLaren.

The Briton started third but endured a difficult opening stint, slipping as far back as P11 as he struggled with straight-line speed and battery deployment in an eventful race that saw 352 overtakes across the field.

Norris began making progress towards the end of his first stint before a mid-race Safety Car, brought out following a collision between Sergio Perez and Rafael Camara, helped him climb to P6. The McLaren driver continued his recovery after the restart, briefly taking the lead before eventually crossing the line just 0.639s behind race winner Max Verstappen, with team mate Oscar Piastri completing the podium.

"I think that must have been the most chaotic race ever in the history of Formula 1," Norris reflected. "I didn't know what was happening half the time. I didn't know if I was going to have the best race and have a chance to win or end up last.

"I had everything in this race. So it was tough. I timed things well in terms of getting back to the front. It was also a race of not making mistakes, like a lot of people made. So, a fun day. Chaotic, but a fun day, and a good result for us as a team."

Speaking in the post-race press conference, Norris explained that managing his battery deployment had been particularly challenging, leaving him vulnerable to overtakes despite having competitive pace throughout the race.

"Every time I got overtaken, I had no battery, someone else had more battery behind, and I just kept dropping back," he explained.

"The whole race was judging battery the whole time. I'm looking at the battery more than I'm looking where I'm going around this track. So it's the most important thing.

"But the second half of the race was very strong in terms of not making mistakes, staying out of the chaos of some of the others around us, and playing things right in the last three or four laps with positioning, slipstreams and battery to give myself the best chance to finish second."

The result marked Norris' seventh podium of the season and his fifth consecutive top-five finish, with the McLaren driver admitting that he had exceeded his expectations heading into the race.

"Today wasn't a race about trying to win. There was no chance we could win the race today," he said. "But P2 was the best, and we achieved it, so I'm happy."

title: A disappointed Arvid Lindblad reflects on the 'strangest thing' that ended his F1 Las Vegas GP
article_text:
A downcast Arvid Lindblad reflects on the moments before the spin that prematurely ended his superb run at the Formula 1 Las Vegas GP.

The rookie left Las Vegas disappointed after looking set for a potential personal best result. The Grand Prix in Sin City began on a bright note for Lindblad, who lined up fifth on the grid. His stunning performance saw him climb to third early on, with high potential for a great result.

However, a spin while attempting to get his cold tyres up to temperature on Lap 20 turned the day around. After the spin, the rookie was unable to get going again and was forced to retire. At the time of the spin, the Racing Bulls driver was running sixth.

Despite the incident being the “strangest thing” he has experienced, the 19-year-old still decided to admit fault for the spin.

“I honestly don’t know what happened,” Lindblad said to media, including Motorsport Week.

“I had a very bad shift, but in the end, it is still my fault; there is no point in blaming that, but it was a very strange feeling and something I’ve not really experienced in the car. I wasn’t doing anything strange; I was very slowly going on throttle, and then I was facing the wall.

“In the end, it’s my fault, and I’ll take it on the chin. But I can’t sit here now and say I understand why, because it was the strangest thing I’ve experienced.”

The night race in Sin City took viewers for a thrilling ride with 352 overtakes, setting the record for the most overtakes in a single F1 race. With the pack tightly bunched, the fight for position was nearly constant.

While he admits the race will be a “difficult one to swallow” because of the missed opportunity, Lindblad still took positives from the early stint. Speaking about the opening stage of the race, Lindblad reflected on the “fun” he had racing against the top teams.

“It was quite fun,” the Racing Bulls driver said. “It’s quite rare that you’re able to fight the top teams. I think it’s just very upsetting that we were in that position and it wasn’t able to capitalise on it.

“It’s going to be a difficult one to swallow because there really was something… I was fortunate to be in a position that we could earn something special today.
